- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows sharp upward trend after a recent dip, check for lag: true price often rises faster than forecast; adjust by adding 1–2% per day to forecasted peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.00) and model forecasts a downtrend, model often underestimates the depth of fall; add 1–3% to forecasted low to account for mean reversion.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast decline at 10% below recent high to avoid overshoot.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates long-term mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecasted mid-range values if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over 5+ days, model tends to overfit recent momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 10–20%.
